summary: The IBK PDF is technically searchable and unclipped, but it conflicts with the reusable artifact's intended applicant-evidence, public-language, reader-comparison, and editorial-design boundaries. The former checks accepted structural PDF success and aggregate scores without proving applicant readiness or reader-facing composition.

findings.observation: All five candidates were marked qualified between 94.90 and 96.30 even though the request retained an unconfirmed IBK-specific motivation, preferred IT domain, direct project contribution, project outcomes, and production-operation experience for the affected questions.
findings.reader_effect: The application answers sound finished while repeatedly admitting that the writer still lacks facts the questions ask the applicant to own.
findings.artifact_conflict: The Skill and contract require material personal gaps to stop or narrow drafting, but the prior schema did not classify an unknown's disposition and the checker allowed a score to compensate in practice.
findings.implemented_control: Every unknown now declares blocking, claim-narrowing, or omitted resolution. A blocking unknown deterministically withholds qualification, and independent review separately records applicant-voice and answer-boundary status.

findings.observation: The searchable text contains 15 occurrences across six report-writer caveat patterns such as facts needing further confirmation or claims the writer will not overstate.
findings.reader_effect: Recruiter-facing prose is interrupted by the report production boundary, making the applicant sound provisional rather than candid and specific.
findings.artifact_conflict: The expression guide already moved generator caveats to the expert report, yet the review marked every answer's public language as pass.
findings.implemented_control: Every candidate-question review now requires applicant-voice and answer-boundary judgments, while blocking facts stop drafting instead of generating disclaimers.

findings.observation: The cover advertises production properties, the question table exposes a closing-method column and machine-oriented values, and repeated running labels describe the report system rather than helping the applicant decide.
findings.reader_effect: The report explains how it was made instead of clarifying what the employer asks and how the applicant should improve the answer.
findings.artifact_conflict: The former semantic review had only one undifferentiated public-label status and recorded no evidence for its pass decision.
findings.implemented_control: Cover purpose, public question-analysis translation, public labels, and production-language separation are distinct non-compensatory review dimensions. Every page and candidate must be named in the independent review with one evidence observation per dimension.

findings.observation: Each candidate start page repeats the set identity and nearly identical title through the numbered section heading, candidate header, set label, title, strategy line, and impression line.
findings.reader_effect: The strongest visual area repeats identity instead of showing the score profile and the meaningful distinction between candidates.
findings.artifact_conflict: The previous profile asked for adjacent score and thesis content but did not define a single primary candidate hierarchy or inspect the rendered DOM.
findings.implemented_control: A candidate start page now permits one primary title, one distinct strategy line, one total, and one complete criterion profile. Continuations may show only a compact continuation heading; normalized title-strategy repetition fails the composition check.

findings.observation: Candidate pages show only total scores. The result contains six weighted dimensions and comments for every candidate, but the rendered report contains no candidate axis table.
findings.reader_effect: Values such as 95.40 and 95.95 cannot be interpreted or compared, so the scoring system provides less decision support than its precision implies.
findings.artifact_conflict: The former profile required criterion-level evaluation data but did not prove that each criterion was visible in the final report.
findings.implemented_control: The composition checker reconciles every candidate's total and every result dimension with a public label, visible weighted score, and explanatory comment in the actual HTML. Missing or unknown rows fail publication.

findings.observation: Pages 7, 8, and 9 occupy approximately 35.5%, 28.5%, and 33.7% of usable body height. Candidate start pages occupy about 64.6% to 67.1%, while continuation pages rise to about 70.5% to 72.0%.
findings.reader_effect: Short internal stages receive full pages while dense answers use very small type, producing an uneven reading rhythm and unnecessary page turns.
findings.artifact_conflict: The old renderer checked clipping but not page purpose, occupied height, candidate continuity, or coherent page-break units.
findings.implemented_control: Every page now declares a role with a role-specific minimum occupied-height ratio. Candidate pages must remain contiguous, and answers, score profiles, figures, and expert-review units use break-inside protection before text size is reduced.

findings.observation: The report has no marked external profile stylesheet, embeds one style element, and uses 18 inline style attributes.
findings.reader_effect: Typography, spacing, and page layout can drift from one report builder to another even when both claim to use the same profile.
findings.artifact_conflict: The former instructions named a CSS file but did not prove that it was the single source of visual styling.
findings.implemented_control: The profile stylesheet must be linked once with a marker. Style elements and inline style attributes fail composition. The stylesheet now exposes reusable typography, spacing, rule, and measure tokens plus candidate, score, continuation, and figure classes.

findings.observation: Three PNG images are registered, but the report contains no figure element, caption, searchable text-equivalent binding, artifact-to-placement binding, or measured figure role. Some visuals restate nearby rows or tables.
findings.reader_effect: Images increase visual weight without consistently adding a relationship that can be understood, searched, or reused at report scale.
findings.artifact_conflict: The old profile counted PNG files but did not validate why, where, or at what size they appeared.
findings.implemented_control: Every raster is now placed once inside a section-bound figure with artifact ID, purpose, relation, alt text, caption, searchable equivalent, and measured width and height ratios. Detached or duplicate-decoration use fails semantic review.

findings.observation: The final page lists the posting, public-sector portal, company blog, five portfolio links, and a secondary prior-question source.
findings.reader_effect: The report ends as a research inventory rather than a focused submission-preparation document.
findings.artifact_conflict: The old request used one visible-source allowlist without distinguishing research admission from public source presentation.
findings.implemented_control: The default public source scope now exposes official posting sources only. A broader source list requires an explicit request-level allowlist.

design_basis.applied_principle: Headings describe topic or purpose and make document organization understandable.
Page fragmentation uses break controls, widows, and orphans to keep coherent content units together.
Typography, spacing, measure, and color use constrained reusable tokens rather than report-specific values.
Long-form text uses readable body size, controlled measure, left alignment, and sufficient leading.
Informative images have equivalent text and decorative images do not add reading noise.
PDF-oriented documents preserve logical heading hierarchy, reading order, table headers, and image alternatives.

residual_limitations: The existing IBK PDF was retained as the diagnostic target and was not regenerated by this artifact-hardening task.

Semantic judgments such as whether a cover sentence describes reader purpose or whether a figure merely restates adjacent content still require independent review; the updated review must name every page and candidate and provide criterion-specific observations.
Occupied-height thresholds are profile defaults for the standard A4 report and may be revised only through a new profile with its own validation evidence.
